page: UpCloud PREMIUM-64xCPU-384GB is a high-capacity virtual instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. Featuring 64 physical cores presenting 64 vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 384 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation of 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include comprehensive instruction set support such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The system includes 500 GB of bundled local SSD storage and one public IPv4 address, operating without dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier across synthetic and real-world compute metrics. The server scored 26,285 in Geekbench multi-core testing, complemented by a single-core score of 2,849, while the PassMark CPU test reached 95,708.23. High-throughput data processing is reflected in single-threaded gzip compression at 44.48 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 923.7 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth registers at 312.37 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, supporting substantial memory transactional workloads, including Redis SET operations measured at 164.99 million operations per second. CPU-based machine learning benchmarks indicate 303.88 prompt tokens per second and 44.24 generation tokens per second on a 7B model.

Architectural tradeoffs center on resource balance and multi-tenancy. The CPU operates under a shared allocation model, and the PassMark memory evaluation places the subsystem in the middle 50% category. In addition, the 500 GB SSD storage volume is modest relative to the 64-core compute capacity and 384 GB memory pool, which may necessitate supplementary network volumes for data-intensive storage footprints. In terms of qualitative efficiency, the high core density and memory ratio deliver strong processing aggregation per instance, making it well-matched for parallel compilation, distributed database engines, in-memory caching systems, and enterprise web serving.

Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compute, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 26,285 and a PassMark CPU score of 95,708.23, combined with Redis SET throughput of 164.99 million operations per second.
